incidents.victim: France — Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: Attacker used a stolen or misused identity in late June to reach internal servers, then connected to the agency's VPN and abused an internal lookup tool to search and extract records.
incidents.impact: France's tax authority confirmed an intrusion; a hacker using the alias ZeroBytes claims to have stolen data on more than 600,000 people and businesses, including names, tax IDs, emails and tax-status details. Affected parties are being notified individually.

incidents.vector: Over four days in November 2023 the group exploited a vulnerability in a payment provider and used cloned payment cards to make unauthorized withdrawals, then laundered funds through Brazil and four European countries.
incidents.impact: German and Brazilian police arrested seven suspects (Operation Klonen) tied to an estimated €30M ($34.7M) drained from German online-banking customers; courts ordered seizure of over $20M in assets. The bank said customers would not bear losses.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government networks; Thailand Ministry of Finance
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese operators chained publicly available AI agents (a Hermes and OpenClaw framework) to automate reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement and data exfiltration against government networks.
incidents.impact: Researchers describe the Taiwan intrusion as the first observed 'near-autonomous' AI-driven attack on a government target, part of a wider wave that also breached Thailand's finance ministry.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion that encrypted and disrupted ministry systems.
incidents.impact: The attack took down systems tied to the ministry's illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes, striking five days before the country's presidential handover.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack that disrupted the court's internal IT systems; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The attack took the Guatemalan Supreme Court's internal systems offline.

incidents.victim: Scotland — Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS)
incidents.vector: A third-party supplier running an online data-maturity assessment for the Scottish government detected suspicious activity on its network on Aug 5, exposing government employee data.
incidents.impact: Names, roles and work email addresses of about 300 COPFS employees were leaked via the contractor; case, victim and witness data were unaffected, though other Scottish agencies used the same assessment and may be affected.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT administrators and their employers
incidents.vector: GRU operators posed as recruiters on job portals, moved contact to Telegram, and used fake interview tasks that required downloading trojanized apps carrying Windows and Linux malware.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's CERT says the campaign (tracked as UAC-0145, a Sandworm sub-group) began in May and is ongoing, aiming to harvest credentials from IT professionals and pivot into the networks they manage.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in the MyDr application to steal customer files and source code.
incidents.impact: MyDr, used by Polish hospitals and reportedly storing data on nearly 19 million people, was breached and the stolen data is being sold online; authorities are investigating.

incidents.victim: CEVA Logistics and downstream European retailers
incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to CEVA's systems and began leaking stolen customer data on a dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: The breach disrupted freight delivery across large parts of Europe, causing days- to weeks-long shipping delays; affected clients include Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf.

incidents.vector: Three separate intrusions into the office's systems that went undetected.
incidents.impact: Reporting revealed that three intrusions at the UK criminal records office went undetected for two years, raising concerns about exposure of sensitive records.

incidents.vector: Gunra affiliates gain initial access by exploiting known vulnerabilities in internet-facing devices (including Fortinet firewall/VPN flaws), then use a Conti-derived double-extortion locker to steal and encrypt data.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA and Korea's KNPA issued a joint #StopRansomware advisory on the Gunra ransomware-as-a-service operation, which recruits pen-testers as access brokers, shows tool overlap with North Korean actors, and has hit victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into port IT systems; the nature of the attack and affected systems were not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted gate operations at the Port of Wilmington, Port of Morehead City and Charlotte Inland Port, forcing manual processing before operations returned to normal; the U.S. Coast Guard and state agencies are investigating.

incidents.victim: U.S. water and wastewater utilities (12 states)
incidents.vector: Intrusions into internet-exposed control systems at local water utilities, manipulating pumps and control panels.
incidents.impact: Attacks spread from seven to at least 12 U.S. states; Clayton County, Georgia customers lost water pressure overnight and pumps ran dry in Duchesne, Utah, where control panels falsely reported normal operation. Iranian hackers are assessed to be behind the intrusions.

incidents.victim: Hungary — State Treasury (Agricultural and Rural Development Office)
incidents.vector: The hacker known as ByteToBreach exploited an unpatched Oracle WebLogic server, exfiltrated data, then deployed a brittle ransomware strain.
incidents.impact: Hungary's State Treasury confirmed the breach; local reporting rated it 10/10 in severity and access. Officials say it hit only the Agricultural and Rural Development Office and no data was wiped; encrypted systems were isolated. The same actor previously wiped Romania's land registry.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a firmware vulnerability that generated weak, easily guessable private keys on Coldcard hardware wallets.
incidents.impact: An estimated $70M–$130M in Bitcoin was stolen from Coldcard users; Coinkite issued a firmware fix, destroyed remaining inventory of affected models, and urged owners to generate new seeds, but the flaw is still being exploited against unpatched users.

incidents.victim: npm open-source ecosystem (keyv, cacheable-request and 400+ packages)
incidents.vector: A self-propagating worm (ChainDrop / Mini Shai-Hulud) compromised a maintainer's GitHub account, injected a preinstall dropper into packages, harvested cloud, npm, GitHub, SSH and CI credentials (including from GitHub Actions runner memory), and republished infected packages using stolen tokens.
incidents.impact: In under four hours the worm infected 400–860 npm packages with a combined 2 billion+ monthly installs; core packages are present in nearly half of all cloud environments. It persists via VS Code and Claude Code hooks and reconfigured its C2 through a single Ethereum transaction.

incidents.vector: INC ransomware chained two SonicWall zero-days (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410) to gain full access, then stole and encrypted data for extortion.
incidents.impact: INC emerged as the most active group weaponizing the SonicWall flaws after their July disclosure, listing alleged victims in Australia, the U.S., UAE, Colombia and Switzerland; researchers prevented data theft in most observed cases but confirmed at least one ransomware deployment.

incidents.victim: Hotels, conference centers and other organizations (global)
incidents.vector: The group compromised WiFi gateways and altered DNS traffic to redirect users to Microsoft-themed phishing pages and ClickFix malware downloads, deploying the CornFlake RAT and CocoShell infostealer and stealing device/OAuth codes to bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: Microsoft attributes the campaign (Storm-2945, part of the SVR-linked Midnight Blizzard cluster) to a wave larger than first reported, targeting hotels and many other organizations since May and reportedly using AI in parts of the operation.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the national business register database holding beneficial-ownership details.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole roughly 31,000 records identifying the de facto owners of companies, foundations and trusts registered in Liechtenstein — a significant exposure given the country's population of about 41,000.
